topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancers within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk, bad luck and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about cancer risk informs the debate over environmental causation versus unavoidable chance.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage capable of becoming mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Context-dependent susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the mechanistic discussion by showing how carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context of exposure.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenicity and linking exposures to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how researchers establish evidence of carcinogenic effects and evaluate the limitations of that evidence.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing their implications for everyday risk–benefit decisions.
